To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

non-planar PCB congeners inhibit migration of NCC in a structure-dependent manner, that the toxicity of PCBs to NCC is linked to the cellular re-distribution and gap junctional inhibition of connexin 43, and that this mechanistic endpoint is useful for the development of a new screening test.

non-ortho-cholorinated PCBs (i.e. non-planar PCB congeners), but not ortho-cholorinated PCB congeners, inhibited migration of neural crest cells, and that the toxicity of non-ortho-chlroinated PCBs correlated with connexin 43 re-distribution in neural crest cells.

the migration-inhibition of neural crest cells assay can be used to identify non-planar PCB congeners as developmental toxicants, and that this effect is mechanistically linked to the cellular re-distribution and the inhibition of gap junctions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to elucidate mechanisms of action, which is of high relevance for the assessment of the risk of chemicals for humans and the environment.
the identification of a new toxicity mechanism, which is linked to a specific chemical structure.
a novel, mechanistic approach to structure–activity relationships.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
non-planar PCB congeners inhibit migration of NCC by interfering with connexin function, which may be linked to the observed developmental neurotoxicity.
non-planar PCB congeners inhibit NCC migration, which is linked to connexin43 re-distribution and gap junctional inhibition.

the toxicity of non-planar PCB congeners is mediated by a disruption of connexin-based cell–cell communication in NCC, and that the cellular re-distribution pattern of connexin 43 is a new mechanistic endpoint that can be used to identify interfering chemicals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cMINC test can be used as a screening method to detect non-planar PCB toxicity, while connexin patterns in NCC can be used as an endpoint to elucidate the underlying mechanisms.
non-planar PCB congeners are toxic to NCC by interfering with gap junctions.
non-planar PCB congeners inhibit NCC migration via gap junction inhibition, and that connexin43 is the key mediator of this effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the establishment of two SARs, one linking chemical structure to a phenotypically relevant endpoint, and one linking chemical structure and phenotypic endpoint to a mechanistic step, may be a powerful strategy to identify relevant mechanisms of action of chemicals.
a double-SAR strategy can be useful to link chemical structures to toxicity mechanisms.
mechanistic information can be obtained from phenotypic test data by using a double-SAR strategy.
